source_prompts.historical_generation: Experiment 19 retains the four REAL ASD/TD prompt pairs. Its package does not retain a complete provider response transcript or model-version metadata; no new LLM call is claimed for Experiment 35.
source_prompts.use: Frozen domain semantics only. Pair rules below are a conservative human synthesis from the retained prompt content and cited studies, not text attributed verbatim to GPT-4.

prompts.D1: Autism spectrum disorder has been investigated in relation to heterogeneous functional connectivity differences involving temporal and temporoparietal systems associated with social information processing.
prompts.D2: Research on autism has examined variable frontoparietal connectivity patterns potentially related to executive control and attention regulation.
prompts.D3: Autism research has investigated heterogeneous thalamocortical and sensorimotor connectivity patterns in relation to sensory processing differences.
prompts.D4: Autism studies have explored differences in cingulate and insular connectivity potentially associated with salience and internal signal processing.

feature_mapping.interpretation_boundary: Domains are candidate measurement ranges anchored to verified HO endpoints. They are not complete canonical networks, validated ASD lesions, or direct inter-network FC measurements. Pair features are co-deviations across domain scores only.

relation_rules.rule: Retain an undirected concept-level joint-deviation relation between frontoparietal/executive and cingulate-insular/salience candidate scores. Evaluate all four signed combinations without imposing a common ASD direction.

paper.citation: Coactivation pattern analysis reveals altered salience network dynamics in children with autism spectrum disorder (2021)
paper.finding: Dynamic coactivation configurations of the midcingulo-insular network with central-executive/lateral-frontoparietal systems appeared less frequently in the ASD group than TD.
paper.supports: A disease-relevant dynamic interaction hypothesis between salience-related and executive/frontoparietal systems.
paper.does_not_support: A universal direction for static FC edges, the exact Experiment 19 HO feature sets, or a direct correlation between the two domain deviation scores.

relation_rules.measurable_with_current_features: Separate signed deviations can be computed for the frozen D2 and D4 FC feature sets and combined into four concept-level co-deviation channels. This measures joint occurrence, not network coactivation or a physical between-network edge.
relation_rules.reason: The primary ASD study directly analyzes salience-midcingulo-insular and central-executive/lateral-frontoparietal coactivation; the current features support only a conservative concept-level test.

relation_rules.rule: Retain an undirected concept-level joint-deviation relation between thalamocortical/sensorimotor and cingulate-insular/salience candidate scores. Evaluate all four signed combinations without imposing a common ASD direction.

papers.citation: Associations between thalamocortical functional connectivity and sensory over-responsivity in infants at high likelihood for ASD (2023)
papers.finding: Thalamic connectivity maps included sensory/motor, middle cingulate, insula and related regions; connectivity related to sensory over-responsivity in an infant high-likelihood design.
papers.supports: A cautious hypothesis that thalamocortical/sensory and cingulo-insular signals can jointly relate to sensory processing.
papers.does_not_support: A diagnosed-ASD-specific direction, current-sample patient labels, or a direct edge represented in the frozen feature set.

papers.citation: Salience Network Connectivity in Autism Is Related to Brain and Behavioral Markers of Sensory Over-Responsivity (2016)
papers.finding: Within ASD, sensory over-responsivity related to right anterior-insula connectivity with somatosensory/sensorimotor and temporal areas.
papers.supports: A sensory phenotype-specific salience-to-sensory interaction hypothesis.
papers.does_not_support: A universal ASD effect or a direct relation between all D3 and D4 candidate features.

relation_rules.measurable_with_current_features: Separate signed deviations can be computed from D3 and D4 support sets and combined into four concept-level co-deviation channels. The two shared mapped feature slots (38 and 218) are not direct thalamus-insula connections; no cross-network FC edge is inferred.
relation_rules.reason: Two primary studies connect thalamic/sensory and insular/salience evidence to sensory processing, while the protocol treats this as a hypothesis about co-deviation rather than direct network coupling.
